title: Human Brain Nuclei Isolation Using Sucrose Gradient Ultracentrifugation
author: Zhang Lab

steps.title: Prepare tissue pieces on dry ice
steps.instruction: Remove brain tissue samples from the –80 °C freezer, place them on dry ice, transfer each sample to a petri dish, cut a small piece with a sterile surgical blade while keeping it on dry ice, place the piece in a labeled Eppendorf tube on dry ice, and return the remaining tissue to its original container; use a fresh petri dish and blade for each sample.

steps.title: Weigh tissue (optional)
steps.instruction: If desired, weigh each Eppendorf tube containing the tissue piece and record the weight; aim for approximately 50 mg per sample.

steps.title: Prepare homogenization buffer with RNase inhibitor
steps.instruction: For each sample, pipette 25 mL of sucrose homogenization buffer into a 50 mL Falcon tube kept on ice, add 1 µL of RNase Inhibitor (40 U/µL) per mL of buffer (i.e., 25 µL per tube), and shake gently to mix.

steps.title: Homogenize tissue in Dounce grinder
steps.instruction: Transfer 15 mL of the homogenization buffer containing RNase Inhibitor into a 15 mL Dounce tissue grinder kept on ice, add the tissue piece, and homogenize as follows:

substeps.instruction: Break large pieces with 3–4 slow up‑and‑down strokes.
Dounce 10 strokes with the loose pestle.
Dounce 10 strokes with the tight pestle.
Pull the pestle out slowly to avoid spilling.

steps.title: Layer homogenate over cushion in ultracentrifuge tube
steps.instruction: Label the bottom of a thin‑wall 50 mL Beckman ultracentrifuge tube (catalog 344058), add 10 mL of fresh homogenization buffer as a cushion, then carefully pour the 15 mL homogenate on top to create two distinct layers.

steps.title: Balance tubes and load into swing bucket
steps.instruction: Place the prepared ultracentrifuge tubes into swing‑bucket rotors, add a few drops of fresh homogenization buffer to the top of each tube as needed to achieve balance, and ensure the buckets are evenly weighted before centrifugation.

steps.title: Ultracentrifuge and clean glassware
steps.instruction: Centrifuge at 25 000 rpm, 4 °C for 1 hour using a SW28 swinging‑bucket rotor (do not use a fixed‑angle rotor). After the run, wash all glassware by rinsing each piece with tap water 10 times, then with Milli‑Q water 5 times, lay out to dry on paper towels, rinse once with DNase‑ and RNase‑free water, air‑dry, and store for future use.

steps.title: Add RNase inhibitor to nuclei suspension buffer
steps.instruction: Prepare 5 mL of nuclei suspension buffer per sample and add 2 µL of RNase Inhibitor (40 U/µL) per mL of buffer (total 10 µL per sample); mix gently and keep on ice.

steps.title: Remove supernatant and cut tube
steps.instruction: After centrifugation, pour off all supernatant into a petri dish, briefly invert the tube upside‑down in the dish, and cut off the wall of the thin‑wall ultracentrifuge tube with a clean razor blade.

steps.title: Resuspend nuclei pellet in buffer
steps.instruction: Resuspend the nuclei pellet at the bottom of the cut tube in 500 µL nuclei suspension buffer, pipette gently up and down 10–20 times, transfer this suspension to a labeled Eppendorf tube, repeat with an additional 500 µL buffer, and keep the tubes on ice.

steps.title: Dilute nuclei with Trypan Blue and count
steps.instruction: In a new labeled Eppendorf tube, mix the nuclei suspension 1:1 with Trypan Blue, load the mixture onto a haemocytometer slide (C‑Chip, DHCN015), count nuclei in each of the four corner 4×4 grids, and calculate the average count.

steps.title: Calculate nuclei concentration
steps.instruction: Compute nuclei concentration using: Average count × 2 (for the 1:1 Trypan Blue dilution) × 10⁴ cells/mL.

steps.title: Spin nuclei at 800 x g
steps.instruction: Centrifuge the nuclei suspension at 800 × g, 4 °C, with acceleration and deceleration set to 9, for 10 minutes (00:10:00).

steps.title: Resuspend to 1000 nuclei/µL for 10X
steps.instruction: Carefully remove the supernatant without disturbing the pellet, then resuspend the nuclei in nuclei suspension buffer to achieve a concentration of approximately 1000 nuclei/µL, which is optimal for 10× Genomics library preparation.

steps.title: Verify concentration with Trypan Blue
steps.instruction: Make a fresh 1:1 dilution of the resuspended nuclei with Trypan Blue, recount using the haemocytometer, and confirm that the concentration falls between 700–1200 nuclei/µL (aim for ~50 nuclei per 4×4 grid).

steps.title: Load samples onto 10x Genomics Chromium
steps.instruction: Submit the verified nuclei suspensions for loading on the 10x Genomics Chromium system using the Single Cell 3’ V3.1 chemistry.
